name: [{{env}}] {{job}} has not reported a run in {{window}}
message:
{{job}} has not reported a run in the last {{window}}.

This is the ABSENCE case for a SPARSE job — one whose `selected` counter is legitimately 0 on most runs, because a checkpoint or a novelty gate means a caught-up run finds nothing to do. So this query counts SUBMISSIONS rather than work: `count_not_null` asks only whether the job reported at all, and a run that honestly reported `selected: 0` counts as a run.

THERE IS THEREFORE ONE CAUSE: THE JOB DID NOT RUN.

  1. PUSH-SUBSCRIPTION JOB. Check Cloud Scheduler for the trigger's last attempt and Cloud Run for 5xx/409 on POST /jobs/{{job}}. A 503 that leaves a pubsub-dedupe lease held answers 409 for the next hour, so one transient error can look like a dead schedule (MONEY-1293: news-sync lost ~62h this way on 2026-08-28, and nothing paged).
  2. CLOUD RUN JOB. Check `gcloud run jobs executions list`, then read the EXECUTION's env rather than the job spec. An execution carrying no DD_API_KEY / DD_METRICS_TRANSPORT takes the DogStatsD branch, posts every counter into a port with no sidecar listening, logs `Connection refused`, and reports NOTHING while exiting 0 (MONEY-1278; edgar-bulk-ftd lost `selected: 13255` exactly this way on 2026-09-03).

WHAT THIS VARIANT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASK is whether the selection gate has broken. For a sparse job `selected: 0` IS the designed steady state, and the zero-write monitor reads 0/0 as idle by design — so a permanently empty selection is unalarmed here, on purpose. The STANDING variant (monitor-job-absence.json) makes the opposite call for jobs whose population always has rows, where a zero IS the defect (MONEY-1215).

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: TRUE, and it is a backstop rather than the mechanism. default_zero() makes
the query itself evaluate on silence, so in the normal case this monitor
alerts from its own threshold and never reaches NO DATA. The one case
default_zero cannot cover is a tag combination that has never existed —
a renamed job id, a changed env tag — where there is no series to fill with
zeros. notify_no_data catches that at 3x the window.
This is the opposite call from monitor-latency-p95.json, and deliberately:
that series is empty in states we ship on purpose, so absence there is not
a signal. Here absence IS the signal.
_threshold_rationale: `< 1` on a COUNT OF SUBMISSIONS, not on a sum of work. `count_not_null`
returns the number of points that actually exist in the window, so a run
that reported `selected: 0` contributes 1 and a window with no run at all
THE DISTINCTION IS REAL IN THE DATA, AND THE STANDING QUERY THROWS IT AWAY.
Measured 2026-09-13 against the live org: edgar-bulk-ftd's 2026-09-10
13:30Z run left ONE non-null point whose value is 0.0, while
resend-contact-sync over the same window has NO SERIES AT ALL.
`default_zero(sum:...)` fills the gaps with zeros and makes those two
states identical — which is why that monitor was created 2026-09-06,
went to Alert 11 seconds later, and had never once been OK, while the
table it feeds (us_cusip_map.SEC_FTD, 23,406 rows) was being filled
`.as_count()` for the reason the zero-write template gives: sum() of a
counter without it is a rate average, which can round a single small run
toward zero and page for a run that happened.
_placeholders: {{env}}              Datadog env TAG value — production | qa
{{window}}           alert window — must exceed the MAX GAP BETWEEN RUNS.
For a SPARSE row that is the ONLY constraint, because
this query ignores the VALUE: the longest legitimate
stretch of `selected == 0` does not size it. See the
_no_data_ceiling_rationale: DATADOG CAPS no_data_timeframe AT 4320 MINUTES (72h). Measured, not read:
35 of 37 monitors were refused 400 "No data timeframe must be <= 4320" on
the first live apply. Everything below follows from that ceiling.
notify_no_data only means something when its timeframe EXCEEDS the job's
legitimate maximum gap. Otherwise it fires on a healthy schedule, gets
muted, and the monitor is worse than absent - which is MONEY-1238.
The WINDOW is already sized to exceed that gap (a week-long cron
window < 4320 min -> no_data = min(3x window, 4320), notify TRUE.
72h still exceeds a sub-72h gap, so clamping is safe.
window >= 4320 min -> the gap is at or past Datadog's ceiling and NO
valid timeframe exists. notify FALSE, deliberately.
The 96h jobs are the ones this decides: Fri->Mon is a 72h legitimate gap,
so a 72h no-data alarm would fire EVERY WEEKEND. That is exactly how
_why_default_zero_stays: LOAD-BEARING, and not obviously so — it looks like the thing this
variant exists to remove. `count_not_null` ALONE returns NO SERIES on a
window with no points (measured against the live org over edgar-bulk-ftd's
silent 2026-09-04..09-09 stretch), so the threshold would never evaluate
and the monitor would sit grey instead of alerting — the exact state
MONEY-1359 finding 10 is about. Wrapped in default_zero() the same window
evaluates to a real 0 and `< 1` fires.
Confirmed by a natural experiment already in the estate: on 2026-09-12
resend-contact-sync's ABSENCE monitor (default_zero) read Alert while its
ZERO-WRITE monitor (no default_zero) read No Data on the very same silence.
